title: Section 2A orders the Fed to promote maximum employment, stable prices, and moderate long-term interest rates
summary: Section 2A orders the Fed to promote maximum employment, stable prices, and moderate long-term interest rates.
body: Section 2A of the Federal Reserve Act, as the Board publishes it, says the Board and the FOMC shall maintain long-run growth of the monetary and credit aggregates commensurate with the economy's long-run potential to increase production, so as to promote effectively the goals of maximum employment, stable prices, and moderate long-term interest rates. The source says: "tively the goals of maximum employment, stable prices, and moderate long-term interest rates." The statute names three goals. It does not write a numeric inflation rate. The Board's note dates the section to an act of 16 November 1977, later amended.
